title: AnyWork — Your local agents. Anywhere.
description: A browser workspace for local Codex, Claude Code CLI, Claude Desktop Code, DeepSeek Harness and WorkBuddy. See each backend’s setup and acceptance limits.
headline:
Good work.
No fixed address.
intro: Let your agents keep working on your computer. Sign in from a browser or phone, find your computer, and continue the conversation, approvals and work.
demoLabel: The conversation. And everything around it.
demoPrompt: Review the release page and polish the mobile experience.
demoReply: The layout now adapts to smaller screens. I also checked the download links and keyboard navigation.
changeText: The layout follows the screen. The context stays with you.
phonePrompt: Can you run the final checks?
phoneHint: Example approval · no command is executed
manifestoText: Pick up a chat, follow tool activity, review files, and keep the conversation moving. The available controls follow the connected agent’s capabilities.
feature1Text: Stream replies, find earlier messages, steer running work and keep drafts between chats. Tools and subagents have their own place in the conversation.
feature2Text: Respond to an approval, inspect a change, or add an image with your own annotations. Browser notifications bring you back when the work needs attention.
feature3Text: Open files, documents, Git changes and a terminal beside your conversation. Each chat remembers its own set of tabs.
connectText: Sign in on your computer; remote access turns on after the workspace is ready and can be turned off anytime. On your phone or browser, sign in to the same account, choose that computer and confirm its identity.
lanText: First review the introduction, then register or sign in through your system browser. The desktop client prepares the local workspace after sign-in, then turns on remote access by default. You can turn it off anytime.
tunnelText: Open the account page on another device. Your computers appear here with their current status; no server address or access key is needed.
vpnText: Confirm the computer’s identity and open its workspace. Return to My devices at any time; signing out closes your authorized remote session.
routeFoot: Work content is encrypted between your devices. Cloud services receive identity and connection metadata; model requests still use your configured provider.
startTitle: From your desk to your pocket, in three steps.
step1Text: Install the latest AnyWork on your Mac, review its introduction and sign in through your system browser to prepare the workspace.
step2Text: Remote access turns on when your local workspace is ready. You can turn it off in the console and expand active encrypted connections.
step3Text: Use the same account on your phone or browser, choose your device, and continue over an encrypted connection.
downloadText: Install the manager on your computer. Take the workspace with you.

faq1Q: Does the work run on my phone?
faq1A: No. Your agent and tools run on your host computer. Your phone or browser connects to that workspace. The host needs to stay awake and connected.
faq2Q: Can I continue an existing chat?
faq2A: Existing chats depend on the backend and connection. Codex needs compatible sharing interfaces for desktop control; Claude Code CLI uses native session IDs for history and resumption. Claude Desktop Code refers only to local Code sessions, with live control acceptance pending. Harness uses its original gateway. WorkBuddy history is readable in supported formats, while shared execution remains experimental. See the setup guide and support matrix below.
faq3Q: Where do my account and work data live?
faq3A: Logto manages accounts and minimal device settings. CyberGrid exchanges connection information. Remote conversations, files and terminal content remain encrypted between your devices; cloud services still see necessary connection metadata. The desktop client requires sign-in before preparation or a new browser-open action. Already authorized local browser sessions and the standalone CLI remain independent. Remote access turns on by default after sign-in and preparation; you can turn it off on the computer.
faq4Q: What is included in this release?
faq4A: The current source covers Codex, Claude Code CLI, local Claude Desktop Code, DeepSeek Harness and WorkBuddy with different capability and acceptance limits. A listed backend or readable history does not guarantee live control. Published packages retain their release-note scope. Voice, native queue migration and closed-browser push are not included.

howTitle: Your work stays here. You can go anywhere.
howText: AnyWork connects your browser or Android app to agents on your own computer. Your files, tools and working context stay with the host. Available actions depend on the backend and connection.
cliTitle: Prefer the terminal? That works too.
cliText: Run the same service from a portable package. Choose your workspace and connect with the Web client.
cliComment: Run from the extracted resources directory
previewSubtitle: A familiar way back to your work.
accountDemo: Device interface illustration · Not live device status
accountPlatformNote: Account remote access is currently qualified on macOS. The new Android Rust / Tauri client bundles its UI and uses in-app sign-in, with native account and encrypted connection management. Android device validation is pending; the published download may still be the previous entry app. Windows and Linux account endpoints require separate validation.
downloadUpdateNote: Use the latest desktop version. Review the introduction, sign in and prepare the workspace, remote access turns on by default once it is ready and can be turned off anytime. On your phone or the Web, use the same account to select the computer. The desktop console shows active encrypted connections.
openSourceNote: Review the code to understand how data security and privacy are implemented.
agentsText: Connect the tools you use on your computer. Each backend keeps its own sessions and setup; readable history and live control have different requirements.
agentsCodex: CLI-backed work and compatible shared engines, with streaming, approvals and model settings. Desktop sharing depends on version and platform.
agentsClaudeCode: Uses your local Claude Code CLI login. The integration covers native session history and resumption; available chat, model and approval controls follow the backend report.
agentsClaudeDesktop: Local Code in Claude Desktop. Supported persisted history remains readable without a control endpoint. Live writes require a valid native bridge allowed by organization policy; a usable control path has not yet been confirmed, and real desktop control acceptance is still pending. Ordinary scripts cannot enable signature-gated CDP. Ordinary chat, Cowork and cloud sessions are separate.
agentsHarness: Connects to the official 0.2.2-rc.1 gateway and original native sessions. Includes history, streaming and approvals; goal/plan, fork and message editing are unavailable.
agentsWorkBuddy: Persisted desktop history, plus experimental shared execution. Real desktop writing, approvals and cancellation still have acceptance gaps.
agentsNote: Current source scope. Published packages follow their release notes. Connection readiness and available actions come from your host; simulated checks do not establish real model or desktop control acceptance.
agentsInstallCli: Install Claude Code CLI from the official setup guide, complete its native sign-in as the host user, and check that claude --version works where AnyWork runs. Then choose Claude Code when the host reports it ready.
agentsInstallDesktop: Install Claude Desktop, sign in and open Code with a local project folder. Desktop uses the same engine as the CLI, with its own session list and independently updated copy of Claude Code. Updating the terminal CLI does not update Desktop’s engine. Signing in does not establish an AnyWork control connection.
agentsHandoff: The official /desktop or claude --desktop command hands work into Desktop; it does not give AnyWork control of an arbitrary running desktop session. See the guide for version, platform and sign-in requirements.
